fields.spec_version: ARINC Specification 429 — Mark 33 Digital Information Transfer System (DITS); reference issue Part 1-17 (Annapolis, Maryland: Aeronautical Radio, Inc., 2004-05-17)
previous_versions: ARINC 429 Mark 33 DITS — original Part 1; incremental updates Part 1-1 through Part 1-17 over decades of avionics deployment.
ARINC 419 — earlier digital data transfer standard, superseded by 429 on higher-end aircraft.
MIL-STD-1553 — contemporary military multidrop serial bus (1973); 429 is the civil-avionics alternative.

key_changes.summary: Defined 32-bit word format (Label / SDI / Data / SSM / Parity), BRZ encoding on shielded 78 Ω twisted-pair, two standard bit rates (12.5 / 100 kbit/s), single-transmitter ≤ 20-receiver topology, BNR / BCD / Discrete data encodings, SSM matrix per encoding.
Reference issue widely cited for label assignments (Sections 78-116) and the canonical wire-level definitions reproduced in commercial-controller datasheets (Holt, AIM, Condor).
Layered on top of ARINC 429 physical layer to define high-speed data loader protocol for software upload.
TDMA-based multi-transmitter extension to ARINC 429; intended to replace 429 but largely superseded by ARINC 664 / AFDX.
Deterministic switched Ethernet replacement for ARINC 429 on newer airframes (Airbus A380, Boeing 787); virtual point-to-point links replace physical 429 buses.
Weather-radar protocol; simplified version of MIL-STD-1553; control of 708 components is standardized through ARINC 429 labels.
Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) interface spec; among other interfaces, defines ARINC 429 interfacing in EFB context.

backward_compat_traps.spec_required: Bit 1 is the first bit transmitted on the wire and is the LSB of the Label octal value (label MSB-first means Label-MSB is on Bit 1 numerically within the label field MSB-1 numbering).
backward_compat_traps.supplier_practice: Some suppliers (AIM GmbH, Condor Engineering) renumber the bit transmission order as '8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,9,10,11,...,32' (LSB-0 within the label octet) to align with octet-oriented shift-register hardware.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hardware programmed with a 'reversed label' octet (e.g. label 0o213 written to the Label byte as 0xD1) interoperates correctly on the wire only because the renumbering is purely a software/diagram convention; mixing tools that use opposite conventions causes label-table lookups to disagree.

backward_compat_traps.spec_required: SSM (bits 30-31) encoding is data-representation-dependent: BCD: 00=+/N/E/R/To/Above, 01=NCD, 10=FT, 11=-/S/W/L/From/Below; BNR: 00=FW, 01=NCD, 10=FT, 11=NO; Discrete: 00=NO, 01=NCD, 10=FT, 11=FW.
backward_compat_traps.receiver_required: Receiver must know the per-label encoding (BCD vs BNR vs Discrete) to decode SSM correctly.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mis-classifying a BCD label as BNR causes SSM=00 to be misread as Failure Warning instead of Plus/N/E/R/To/Above (or vice versa).

backward_compat_traps.equipment_practice: Equipment commonly tolerates 12-14.5 kbit/s on the low-speed bus.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mixing a strict 12.5 kbit/s receiver with a transmitter at the 14.5 kbit/s edge may exit the BRZ eye at the receiver's sample point.
Exceeding 20 receivers degrades the BRZ rise/fall times and parallel input impedance below the 78 Ω budget; receivers near the bus end see slewed transitions.

fields.version_naming_history_note: ARINC 429 is the predominant avionics serial data bus on most higher-end commercial and transport aircraft, deployed since the late 1970s. Newer airframes (Airbus A380, Boeing 787) migrate to AFDX (ARINC 664 Part 7) deterministic Ethernet, retaining ARINC 429 only for legacy interfaces. ARINC 419 was the predecessor; MIL-STD-1553 is the contemporary military equivalent. 429 is unidirectional simplex; bidirectional avionics traffic requires a pair of 429 buses or an ARINC 629 / 664 / 615 extension.
